title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a projective scheme, K(X) its Grothendieck group of locally free (or coherent) sheaves, γ: {sheaves} → K(X) the class map, and M ⊂ K(X) a subset. Grothendieck is defining what it means for a subset of K(X) to be 'bounded' (limité). He gives three conditions and claims they are equivalent.

(i) There are bounded families of locally free sheaves (F_i), (G_i) on X such that M ⊂ {γ(F_i) − γ(G_i)}. The marginal note 'loc. libres' was inserted here.

(ii) There exist integers n, N and a finite set P ⊂ Q[T] such that every x ∈ M has the form γ(F) − γ(G). Here F and G are locally free quotients of O(−n)^N whose Hilbert polynomials lie in P.

(iii) The Hilbert polynomials of the ξ ∈ M (defined on K(X) by χ(ξ(m))) are finitely many. Moreover there are locally free A and B (for instance B = O(−n)^N) such that each ξ + γ(A), for ξ ∈ M, is the class of a locally free quotient of B. The bracketed finiteness clause, inserted in a box, is necessary. Without it, (iii) fails to imply boundedness: on P^1 the line bundles O(d), d ≥ 0, are all quotients of O^2 but form no bounded family.

Proofs sketched:
- (iii) ⇒ (ii) is trivial, since A and B are themselves quotients of some O(−n)^N.
- (ii) ⇔ (i) follows from the characterization of bounded families. A family of sheaves is bounded iff, after a uniform twist, its members are quotients of a fixed O(−n)^N with finitely many Hilbert polynomials. This uses uniform Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity in one direction, and in the other the Quot scheme being of finite type with an open locally-free locus.
- (ii) ⇒ (iii): write G = O(−n)^N / R with R locally free, being the kernel of a surjection between locally free sheaves. Then ξ = γ(F) − γ(O(−n)^N) + γ(R), so ξ + γ(O(−n)^N) = γ(F ⊕ R). Grothendieck's 'F+R' is the direct sum. Since the R form a bounded family (kernels in a bounded family of quotients), F ⊕ R is uniformly a quotient of some O(−n')^{N_1}. The page breaks off here.

Purpose: this is preparatory for the next page. There X is assumed nonsingular and M' ⊂ Z^i(X) is a group of cycles modulo K-equivalence. He compares several notions:
- algebraically bounded families of cycles;
- numerically bounded families, together with a positivity condition ξ_0 + ξ being a limit of positive cycles;
- images of bounded subsets of K(X) under (i−1)!·(Chern character)/c^i.

The context (cote 14) is the standard conjectures and algebraic cycles. The aim is a boundedness formulation for cycles, transported from K-theory, where boundedness is well understood via Quot schemes.
errors: Condition (iii) as first written (fixed A, B, without finiteness of Hilbert polynomials) does not imply (ii): quotients of a fixed locally free B need not form a bounded family. Grothendieck evidently noticed this and inserted the clause 'Les polynômes de Hilbert des ξ ∈ M en nombre fini'. With that clause the equivalence is correct.

In (ii) ⇒ (iii) the step 'F ⊕ R is a quotient of O(−n)^{N_1}' needs uniform regularity of the kernels R. This follows from boundedness of the Quot scheme but is not spelled out; the page breaks off mid-sentence.
(iii) ⇒ (ii) is only 'trivial' given the finiteness of Hilbert polynomials and the fact that the A-twist shifts Hilbert polynomials by a fixed amount. This is fine but implicit.

ideas.what: Notion of a bounded (limité) subset of K(X): differences of classes of members of bounded families of locally free sheaves, with equivalent characterizations via quotients of O(−n)^N and finitely many Hilbert polynomials
ideas.modern_name: boundedness of sets of K-classes / bounded families via Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity and Quot schemes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (FGA, Hilbert/Quot schemes); Mumford (regularity, 1966); Kleiman (SGA 6 Exp. XIII, boundedness)
ideas.where_published: Characterization of bounded families: FGA exposé 221 and SGA 6 Exp. XIII (Kleiman). An explicit notion of bounded subsets of K(X) is not known to me in print.

ideas.what: Normalization trick: shift a bounded set of K-classes by a fixed γ(A) so that all elements become classes of actual locally free quotients of a fixed B, using G = O(−n)^N/R ⇒ ξ + γ(O(−n)^N) = γ(F ⊕ R)
ideas.modern_name: representing virtual classes by honest bundles after a uniform shift

missed.claim: The page sets up a K-theoretic notion of boundedness. It is meant to be compared, on the next page, with algebraic, numerical and positivity-based boundedness of codimension-i cycles via Chern classes. This is a program for 'numerically bounded ⇒ algebraically bounded' for higher-codimension cycles, related to the standard conjectures. The K-theoretic part on this page is routine and complete, but the cycle-theoretic comparison was not carried out in print as far as I know. Later work (Griffiths, Clemens: infinitely generated Griffiths groups) shows that naive versions of such comparisons must fail modulo algebraic equivalence.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It documents Grothendieck trying to formulate boundedness conjectures for cycles through K-theory and Quot-scheme boundedness. The mathematics on this page itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but routine lemma on boundedness of subsets of K(X) using standard Quot-scheme and regularity arguments. Its only interest is as groundwork for a boundedness program for algebraic cycles on the following page.
transcription_corrections: 'F + R' should be read as the direct sum F ⊕ R.
In (iii) the boxed insertion reads 'Les polynômes de Hilbert des ξ ∈ M en nombre fini et'. It is a substantive hypothesis, not a stray remark.
The parenthesis in (iii) reads 'A et B (O(−n)^N disons)', i.e. B is meant to be O(−n)^N.

The final line reads roughly 'Or F+R est un quotient de O(−n)^{N_1}, dans les F+R sont quotients d'un…' and the page breaks off. The intended phrase is likely 'car les F+R forment une famille limitée'.
